summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore (until 1992) and the University of Amsterdam (until 2000). Working in Indology, he held posts at FRLHT (1995), Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama (1998, 2003–2004).

Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu and with Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1908). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo and Taisho University (~1926–1937).

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. She has served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin, working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology, completed her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~2003–2009). She has held posts at UC Berkeley, National University of Mongolia (2013–2014), IUPUI (~2019), Yonsei University, and the University of Iceland.

Urs App (born 1949) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Fribourg and Temple University. Mentored by Yoshitaka Iriya, Richard DeMartino, and Seizan Yanagida, he worked at Hanazono University and EFEO.

Ute Hüsken (born 1965) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. She completed her dissertation under Heinz Bechert at the University of Göttingen (~1988–1995) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~2003–2008).

V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras (1931–1934). He spent his academic career at the University of Madras, serving in the Sanskrit Department and as its head.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there attested in 2018.

Vajragupta (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as director at the Birmingham Buddhist Centre (1997) and held a directorship within the Triratna Buddhist Community (attested 2010).

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University (~1948–1956), later holding posts at Meiji Gakuin University, Princeton University (~1960–1965), and the University of Hawaii (~1965–1995).

Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She wrote her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kvaerne (attested 2009).
Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1854–1858) and held a post at the Kunstkamera (~1894–1918).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Principal and Professor of Sanskrit at Morris College (~1919–1947) and Government Vidarbha Institute (~1947–1950), and later taught at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (~1957–1966).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (1901–1991) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology scholar. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (1930), he held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi (attested 1966).

Vasudha Narayanan (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the Universities of Madras and Mumbai before completing her education at Harvard (~1974–1978). She was appointed Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982).

Verity Harte (born 1968) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1989–1996). She held an academic post at King's College London (~1997–2005) before joining the faculty at Yale University (~2005).

Vesna A. Wallace (born 1952) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar who completed her doctorate at UC Berkeley. She held positions at UC Berkeley, the University of Oxford (until 2010), and UC Santa Barbara (attested 2007–2014).
Victor B. Lieberman (born 1945) is a historian. He studied at Yale University (~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (~1972–1976), and took up a post at the University of Michigan around 1984.

Victor Chan (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Chicago. He served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (~2005).

Victor Forte is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University in 2004 and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).
